mainTopic: The end of the משנה about believing a person whose own words both create and remove a problem (הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר), and the opening of the גמרא, which asks whether the משנה's ruling about a widow's כתובה contradicts רבן גמליאל.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the משנה. A man who admits a field was his friend's father's, but says he bought it, is believed, because 'the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted.' If witnesses prove the field was the father's, he is not believed. The גמרא then returns to the woman who says she married as a בתולה. It asks whether the משנה, which needs witnesses, goes against רבן גמליאל. The answer is that רבן גמליאל believes her only in a case of ברי ושמא, and here both sides are ברי. The גמרא tries to prove this from the words 'ומודה רבי יהושע'. That proof is pushed off: רבי יהושע is really comparing a מגו in our פרק to a מגו in the first פרק. After testing several first-פרק cases, the גמרא settles on the woman who says she was raped after אירוסין. It explains that a מגו cannot help her because there is already a 'slaughtered ox' in front of us. Finally, the גמרא asks why witnesses are needed if most women marry as בתולות. רבינא begins to answer that a virgin's wedding gets publicity, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains why someone is believed when his only source of trouble is his own admission: the same mouth that created the problem also solved it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is believed, because the same mouth that made it forbidden is the mouth that made it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason for a ruling about someone who says, 'This field was your father's, and I bought it from him.' He is believed because only his own words told us the field was ever the father's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without his admission, nobody would know the field ever belonged to the other person's father. His single statement both raised the problem and answered it. So we cannot use the first half against him while ignoring the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: The mouth, meaning a person's own statement.
That forbade, meaning the words that created the problem.
That permitted, meaning the words that removed the problem.

steps.whyThisMatters: הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר is a basic rule used throughout ש״ס for believing a person whose claim comes entirely from his own testimony.

phrases.english: For the mouth that forbade
is the mouth that permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling at the end of the משנה (stated just before this text begins).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person whose claim rests entirely on his own admission is believed for the whole statement, because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted.

steps.title: When witnesses already prove the field was the father's
steps.stepSummary: If witnesses show the field belonged to the other man's father, the holder's claim that he bought it is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there are witnesses that the field belonged to his father, and the holder says, 'I bought it from him,' he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the limit of the rule. Once witnesses, and not the man himself, prove the field was the father's, he can no longer just say he bought it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem (the field was the father's) comes from the witnesses, not from his own mouth. So the rule of הפה שאסר does not apply. His claim of purchase stands alone without support.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses.
I bought it from him.
He is not believed.

steps.whatToRemember: הפה שאסר works only when your own words are the only source of the problem. Once outside witnesses prove the problem, your explanation is not automatically believed.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל אָבִיו,
phrases.english: But if there are witnesses that it belonged to his father,
and he says, 'I bought it from him,'
he is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the boundary of the rule in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When witnesses establish the original ownership, the holder's claim of purchase is not accepted.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that without witnesses the husband is believed. It asks whether this contradicts רבן גמליאל, who believes the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason she wins is that there are witnesses. So if there are no witnesses, the husband is believed. Shall we say the unnamed ruling of our משנה is not like רבן גמליאל? Because רבן גמליאל said she is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a woman who says she married as a בתולה while her husband says she married as an אלמנה. It reads in the משנה that without witnesses the husband wins, and points out that this looks like it goes against רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives the woman her full כתובה if witnesses saw her wedding procession. So without witnesses the husband must be believed. But in an earlier משנה, רבן גמליאל believed the woman against her husband. That makes it seem our unnamed משנה disagrees with him.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason. It is used to read in the opposite case.
But if there is not. This introduces the opposite case read into the text.
Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא is testing.
An unnamed ruling in the משנה, given without the name of a תנא.
Believed.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not talking about the field case just finished. It jumps back to the first case of the משנה, about the woman's כתובה and the witnesses to her wedding procession (הינומא).

phrases.english: Gemara
The reason is that there are witnesses,
phrases.notes: These are the witnesses who saw her go out to the wedding the way a בתולה does, mentioned earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: but if there are no witnesses, the husband is believed.
Shall we say we learned an unnamed ruling
that is not like Rabban Gamliel?
For if it were Rabban Gamliel,
didn't he say that she is believed!
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier משנה, where she and her husband argue about when she lost her virginity, and רבן גמליאל believes her.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תְּנַן סְתָמָא דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by going back to the first case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The unnamed משנה's ruling that without witnesses the husband is believed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל believes the woman against her husband, so a משנה that believes the husband seems to disagree with him.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל only spoke about ברי ושמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can match רבן גמליאל. He believes the woman only when she is certain and the husband is unsure. Here both are certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבן גמליאל. רבן גמליאל only said she is believed there, in a case of 'certain versus maybe.' But here, where it is 'certain versus certain,' he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that the two cases are different. So there is no argument with רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבן גמליאל's case, the husband cannot really know when she lost her virginity, so his claim is only a guess. Her sure claim beats his guess. In our case, the husband knows for sure whom he married, so both sides are certain. רבן גמליאל's reasoning does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say. It shows the ruling can fit the opinion in question.
He only said his ruling up to this point. It limits an opinion to its own case.
A certain claim against an unsure one.
A certain claim against another certain claim.

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between ברי ושמא and ברי וברי is a key tool in many monetary disputes across ש״ס.

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabban Gamliel.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel only said it there,
in a case of 'certain' against 'maybe.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא בְּבָרִי וּבָרִי — לָא אָמַר.
phrases.english: But here, with 'certain' against 'certain,' he did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to disagree with רבן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל only believes the woman in a case of ברי ושמא. In ברי וברי he agrees the husband is not beaten, so the משנה fits his view.

steps.title: Why did the questioner ask at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why anyone would have raised the earlier question, since the case is obviously ברי וברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who asked it, why did he ask? This is clearly a case of 'certain against certain'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions its own earlier question. The difference between the cases seems so obvious that the question should never have been asked. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can see that the husband here knows for sure whom he married. So the comparison to רבן גמליאל's case looks weak from the start. The גמרא wants to know what the questioner was thinking.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who asked it.
Why did he ask it?

phrases.english: And the one who asked it, why did he ask it?
This is 'certain' against 'certain'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the question of step 3, in light of the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the case is plainly ברי וברי, comparing it to רבן גמליאל's ברי ושמא case seems to make no sense.

steps.title: The majority made it look like ברי ושמא
steps.stepSummary: Because most women marry as בתולות, the woman's claim has the majority behind it. That made the case look like ברי ושמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since most women marry as בתולות, the case seems like 'certain against maybe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the questioner was thinking. The majority supports the woman, which seems to weaken the husband's claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's claim is certain, but it goes against what usually happens, because most brides are בתולות. The questioner thought this majority made the woman's claim so much stronger that it was like a sure claim against a guess. That is why he compared it to רבן גמליאל's case. The answer in step 4 still stands: in the end, it is ברי וברי.

keyTerms.meaning: Since.
The majority, meaning what usually happens.
It is similar to; it is like.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can follow רבן גמליאל. He believes the woman only in ברי ושמא. Our case is ברי וברי, even though the majority of women marrying as בתולות made it look closer to ברי ושמא.

phrases.english: Since most women are married as virgins,
it is like 'certain' against 'maybe.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by explaining the questioner's thinking.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the question was reasonable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question about רבן גמליאל seemed baseless, since the case is ברי וברי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the majority backs the woman, the case resembled ברי ושמא, which made the question reasonable to ask.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'and he concedes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the previous answer from the משנה's wording. The phrase 'ומודה רבי יהושע' suggests that someone conceded before him, and that someone must be רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense that רבן גמליאל concedes here, because the משנה says 'And רבי יהושע concedes.' If רבן גמליאל was conceding in the first case, this fits well: each one concedes something to the other. But if רבן גמליאל was not conceding there, then whom is רבי יהושע conceding to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its last answer. That answer said that even רבן גמליאל agrees the woman is not believed in our case, because both sides are certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ומודה רבי יהושע', 'and רבי יהושע concedes', suggests a matching concession by the other side. The natural candidate is רבן גמליאל, conceding in the first case of the משנה that the woman is not believed, even though the case looks like ברי ושמא. Without that, רבי יהושע's concession seems to have no partner.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too it stands to reason (introduces a supporting proof)
Concedes, admits that the other side is right
It is fine / granted (this option works)
Well, it works nicely
Is speaking about / dealing with

phrases.english: And so too it stands to reason
since the Mishnah teaches, "And Rabbi Yehoshua concedes":
phrases.notes: This is from later in our משנה: someone admits a field was your father's but says he bought it, and רבי יהושע agrees he is believed.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that Rabban Gamliel is speaking as one who concedes, it works well.
But if you say
that Rabban Gamliel is not speaking as one who concedes,
then to whom is Rabbi Yehoshua conceding?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for the answer given in Steps 4–6, which said that רבן גמליאל agrees with our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל concedes the woman is not believed in a case of ברי וברי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'ומודה רבי יהושע' in the משנה, which implies a matching concession by רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's concession refers to the first chapter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יהושע's 'concession' is not tied to this פרק. It is about the principle of מגו and points back to his argument with רבן גמליאל in the first פרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think רבי יהושע's statement refers to this chapter? No. It refers to the idea of מגו, and it points back to the first chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The word 'concedes' does not have to mean that רבן גמליאל conceded something here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פרק, רבי יהושע argued with רבן גמליאל and refused to believe a woman even when she had a מגו. Here, in the field case, he does accept that kind of reasoning ('the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted'). So 'he concedes' means he concedes to רבן גמליאל's approach from the first פרק. It does not prove that רבן גמליאל conceded in this פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think...? (introduces a rejection of an assumption)
Stands on, refers to
'Since' — a person is believed because he could have made a better claim and did not
The first chapter (of כתובות)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'ומודה' can point back across chapters. רבי יהושע concedes the principle of מגו, which he rejected against רבן גמליאל in the first פרק.

phrases.english: Do you think
that Rabbi Yehoshua is referring to this chapter?
He is referring to the principle of 'since' (miggo),
and he is referring to the first chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אַהַאי פִּירְקִין קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 7 by giving the word 'ומודה' a different reference point.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject the earlier answer that רבן גמליאל might agree here.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'ומודה' refers to a concession in this פרק. It can refer to the מגו dispute in the first פרק instead.

steps.title: Which first-chapter case? Trying the pregnant woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case in the first פרק רבי יהושע was referring to. It first suggests the case of the pregnant woman who says the father is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which case is it? Suppose it is this one: a woman was pregnant, and people asked her, 'What is the story of this baby?' She answered, 'It is from a certain man, and he is a כהן.' רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says, 'We do not live by what comes out of her mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now wants to identify the exact case from the first פרק. It quotes the pregnant-woman case as a first suggestion, which sets up the next move where this suggestion will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the answer in Step 8 to work, there has to be a case in the first פרק where the woman has a מגו and רבי יהושע still does not believe her. The pregnant-woman case is the first one tried.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? (which case?)
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will probably be rejected)
Pregnant
What is his nature / story?
We do not live by her word (she is not believed)

phrases.english: On which case? If you say on this one:
She was pregnant,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ ״מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל עוּבָּר זֶה״.
phrases.english: and they said to her, "What is the story of this fetus?"
"It is from a certain man, and he is a kohen,"

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
We do not live by her mouth —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the specific case behind Step 8's claim that רבי יהושע refers to the first פרק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case in the first פרק involves a מגו that רבי יהושע rejected.

steps.title: The pregnant woman has no מגו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the pregnant-woman case. She cannot deny relations, because her pregnancy is obvious, so she has no better claim to give her a מגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in that case, what מגו is there? Her belly is right in front of her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first suggestion. The pregnant woman has no מגו at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מגו needs a better lie she could have told. A pregnant woman cannot say 'I was never with anyone,' because everyone can see she is pregnant. So רבי יהושע's 'concession' about מגו cannot be pointing to this case.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
Literally 'her belly is between her teeth': her pregnancy is obvious

phrases.english: There, what miggo is there?
Her belly is between her teeth!
phrases.notes: This is a picture phrase: her pregnancy is right out in front, so she can't claim she was never with anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם מַאי מִגּוֹ אִיכָּא? הֲרֵי כְּרֵיסָהּ בֵּין שִׁינֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects identifying the pregnant-woman case as the one רבי יהושע referred to.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case there is no better claim available to her, so there is no מגו.

steps.title: Second try: the woman seen speaking with a man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different case from the first פרק instead. A woman was seen 'speaking' with a man and says he is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to this case: people saw her speaking with a man and asked her, 'What is the story of this man?' She said, 'He is a certain man, and he is a כהן.' רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says, 'We do not live by what comes out of her mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the pregnant-woman case failed, the גמרא offers another case from the first פרק as the one רבי יהושע was referring to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This woman is not visibly pregnant. So it seems she might have a better claim available, which could give her a מגו. That would make it a fitting case for רבי יהושע's 'concession' about מגו.

keyTerms.meaning: They saw her
'Speaking' (its exact meaning is debated in the next step)
A certain man, so-and-so

phrases.english: Rather, on this case:
They saw her speaking with a man,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: ״מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל אִישׁ זֶה״.
phrases.english: and they said to her: "What is the story of this man?"
"He is a certain man, and he is a kohen,"

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by her mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַהָא: רָאוּהָ מְדַבֶּרֶת עִם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case from Step 10 with another case from the first פרק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע was referring to the case of the woman seen 'speaking' with a man.

steps.title: Does the 'speaking' case have a מגו for everyone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what מגו she has. It works for זעירי, who explains 'speaking' as being secluded with the man, because she could have denied relations. It fails for רב אסי, who explains 'speaking' as having relations, because then she has no better claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, what מגו is there? That works for זעירי, who says 'speaking' means she was secluded with him. Since she could have said 'I was not with him,' and instead she said 'I was with him,' she is believed. But according to רב אסי, who says 'speaking' means she had relations, what מגו is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second suggestion. It shows that the case has a מגו only according to one of the two explanations of the word 'speaking'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to זעירי, people only saw her secluded with the man. So she could have denied any relations, which was a better claim, and that gives her a מגו. According to רב אסי, she was seen having relations, so she cannot deny it, and there is no מגו. Because this case fails for רב אסי, the גמרא drops it and tries another case in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for... (usually followed by 'but for the other view it does not')
She was secluded (alone) with a man
She had relations
She is believed

steps.confusionAlert: Neither זעירי nor רב אסי reads 'מדברת' as plain talking. They only argue over whether it means being secluded with him or actually having relations.

phrases.english: There, what miggo is there?
This works well according to Ze'eiri, who said:
What does "speaking" mean? She was secluded with him,

phrases.aramaic: מִגּוֹ דְּאִי בָּעֲיָא אָמְרָה לֹא נִבְעַלְתִּי,
phrases.english: since if she wanted, she could have said, "I did not have relations,"
and she says, "I had relations," she is believed.
But according to Rav Asi,
who said: What does "speaking" mean? She had relations,
what miggo is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case proposed in Step 11 by showing that it has no מגו according to רב אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'seen speaking' case is the מגו case רבי יהושע was referring to.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'speaking' means she had relations, as רב אסי says, she could not have denied it. So there is no better claim and no מגו, and the case cannot be the source of a concession about מגו.

steps.title: A new suggestion: the case of the wood injury
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהושע was referring to the case where the woman says she is a מוכת עץ and the husband says she is a דרוסת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant this case: she says, 'I was injured by wood,' and he says, 'No, you were with a man.' רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says we do not live by what comes out of her mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The 'speaking with a man' case did not fully work, so the גמרא offers a new case. It is the argument where she says her בתולים were lost by an injury from wood, and he says she was with a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case has the same form as the others: רבן גמליאל believes her and רבי יהושע does not. If she has a מגו here, this could be the case רבי יהושע meant. The next step tests whether she really has a מגו.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it refers to this case
A woman whose בתולים were lost through an injury, such as from wood, and not through relations
A woman who had relations with a man
She is believed
We do not rely on her word alone

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to this case:
she says: I was injured by wood,
phrases.notes: She means her בתולים were lost by an accident, not by being with a man.

phrases.english: and he says: Not so,
rather, you were trampled by a man.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין —
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by what comes out of her mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new case after the 'speaking' case ran into trouble in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע was referring to the מוכת עץ case.

steps.title: Does she have a מגו in the wood-injury case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what מגו she has in the מוכת עץ case. According to רבי אלעזר there is one, but according to רבי יוחנן there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, what מגו is there? It works for רבי אלעזר, who says the argument is 100 against nothing. She could have said 'I was injured by wood after you betrothed me' and received 200. Since she says it happened before, and so gets only 100, she is believed. But for רבי יוחנן, who says the argument is 200 against 100, what מגו is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new suggestion. It asks whether she has a better claim she could have made instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר she is asking for only 100, when she could have claimed the injury happened after אירוסין and asked for 200. That gives her a מגו. According to רבי יוחנן she is already asking for 200, the most she can get. With no better claim left, there is no מגו, so this case cannot be the one for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well for (this opinion)
One hundred זוז, a smaller כתובה
Two hundred זוז, the full כתובה of a בתולה
Under you, meaning after you betrothed me
From the beginning, meaning before אירוסין

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן are not arguing about the הלכה here. Each one is explaining what the two sides were claiming in the earlier argument, and the מגו depends on that.

phrases.english: There, what מגו is there?
It works for Rabbi Elazar,
who said: the argument is about 100 against nothing.
There is a מגו, since if she wanted, she could have said:
'I was injured by wood while under you,'
and she would have had 200,
and instead she says it happened from the beginning,
where she has only 100, so she is believed.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said:
the argument is about 200 against 100,
what מגו is there?
phrases.notes: She is already asking for the most she could get, so there is no better lie she gave up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the case suggested in Step 13 and finds it works only for רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהושע meant the מוכת עץ case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יוחנן, she is already making her best claim, so she has no מגו to rely on.

steps.title: Another suggestion: raped after betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case of a woman who says she was raped after אירוסין, while the husband says it happened before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant this case: a man marries a woman and does not find בתולים. She says, 'After you betrothed me I was raped, and your field was flooded.' He says, 'No, it happened before I betrothed you.' רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says we do not live by what comes out of her mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third case from the first פרק. Here she says she was raped after אירוסין, and he says it happened before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it happened after אירוסין, it is the husband's bad luck and she keeps her full כתובה. If it happened before, he can say the marriage was a mistake. רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע argue here too, so the גמרא checks whether she has a מגו.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs of virginity
After you betrothed me
I was raped
His field was flooded; a picture for the husband's own bad luck
Before I betrothed you

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to this case:
One who marries a woman
and did not find her a virgin,
she says: 'After you betrothed me, I was raped,
and his field was flooded,'
phrases.notes: This is a way of saying it was the husband's own bad luck, since it happened once she was already his.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא כִי, אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא אֵירַסְתִּיךְ״.
phrases.english: and he says: 'Not so, rather it was before I betrothed you.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by what comes out of her mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the מוכת עץ case, which failed for רבי יוחנן in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע was referring to the case of a woman who says she was raped after אירוסין.

steps.title: Why she has a מגו in the rape case
steps.stepSummary: She could have said she was a מוכת עץ after אירוסין, which would not have disqualified her from כהונה. Instead she said she was raped, which does disqualify her. So רבן גמליאל believes her.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a מגו: if she wanted, she could have said 'I was injured by wood while under you,' which does not disqualify her from כהונה. Instead she said 'I was raped,' which does disqualify her from כהונה. That is why רבן גמליאל says she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the מגו in this case. It shows that this מגו works no matter how you explain the earlier argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both claims place the event after אירוסין, so either way she would get her full כתובה. But saying 'raped' costs her, because it makes her unfit to marry a כהן, while 'wood' would not. Since she picked the claim that hurts her when an easier lie was available, she is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: If she wanted to
She disqualifies herself
The כהנים; here, being allowed to marry a כהן
She is believed

steps.whyThisMatters: This מגו does not depend on how much money is involved. It is about her status, so the רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן question from Step 14 does not come up.

phrases.english: For there is a מגו: since, if she wanted, she could have said
'I was injured by wood while under you,'
where she would not disqualify herself from כהונה.
And instead she says: 'I was raped,'
where she does disqualify herself from כהונה,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דִּמְהֵימְנָא.
phrases.english: therefore Rabban Gamliel says that she is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the מגו in the case suggested in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She had a less harmful claim available (מוכת עץ), so her harmful claim (raped) is believed.

steps.title: רבי יהושע agrees here but disagrees there
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells רבן גמליאל that he agrees about this מגו in our case, but disagrees about the מגו in the case of the first פרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says to רבן גמליאל: about this מגו here, I agree with you. About that מגו there, I disagree with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation of רבי יהושע's 'concession.' He accepts the מגו in our case but not in the first-פרק case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the search that began in Step 9. רבי יהושע's 'concession' does not answer a concession by רבן גמליאל in the first case of our משנה. It compares two kinds of מגו: the one 'here', the field case in our פרק, works. The one 'there', the first-פרק case of the woman who says she was raped, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: I agree with you
I disagree with you
Here / there

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע agrees that a מגו works in our case. He argues with רבן גמליאל only about the case of a woman who says she was raped after אירוסין, where the מגו is that she could have said she was a מוכת עץ.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua says to Rabban Gamliel:
About this מגו here, I agree with you;
about that מגו there, I disagree with you.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the case of the first פרק, the woman who says she was raped after אירוסין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes Step 16 by explaining what רבי יהושע's concession means.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע accepts the מגו here and disputes only the first-פרק case of the woman who says she was raped after אירוסין.

steps.title: Both cases are a מגו, so why treat them differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע. Both the field case and the woman's case rely on a מגו, so why does he accept one and reject the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, this is a מגו and that is a מגו. What is the difference between this מגו and that מגו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע accepts the מגו in our case but rejects the מגו in the case of the first פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, רבי יהושע agreed to one מגו and disagreed about another. Both are built on the same logic: 'she could have made a better claim, so we believe the claim she did make.' The גמרא wants a real reason for treating them differently.

keyTerms.meaning: After all / since (it is clear that)
Since (he could have said a better claim, we believe what he said)
What is the difference?

phrases.english: After all, this is a מגו and that is a מגו,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the case רבי יהושע agreed to, and 'that' is the case of the first פרק he disagreed with (step 17).

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הַאי מִגּוֹ מֵהַאי מִגּוֹ?
phrases.english: what is different about this מגו from that מגו?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי הַאי מִגּוֹ וְהַאי מִגּוֹ מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction רבי יהושע made in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's acceptance of one מגו and rejection of the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases have the same מגו structure, so it seems they should be judged the same way.

steps.title: The slaughtered ox: suspicion already in front of us
steps.stepSummary: In the field case nothing raises a question, so the מגו works. In the woman's case there is already a reason to suspect her, so the מגו does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, there is no slaughtered ox in front of you. There, a slaughtered ox is in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases differ because in one there is already a visible reason for suspicion and in the other there is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the field case, the field is in his possession and nothing makes us doubt him, so a מגו can support him. In the woman's case, she was found not to be a בתולה, which is like a slaughtered ox lying in front of us: a real problem is already there. A מגו is not strong enough to push aside a problem that is already visible.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughtered ox; an image for clear evidence that raises suspicion
In front of you
Here / there

steps.whatToRemember: A מגו works when nothing is raising suspicion. It does not work against a problem that is already in front of us (the 'slaughtered ox').
steps.confusionAlert: The 'ox' is not a real animal in the case. It is a picture for something in front of us that already makes us doubt the claim.

phrases.english: Here, there is no slaughtered ox before you.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the field case, where nothing gives us a reason to doubt the owner.

phrases.english: There, a slaughtered ox is before you.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the woman found not to be a בתולה. The problem is already visible before she makes her claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא אֵין שׁוֹר שָׁחוּט לְפָנֶיךָ הָתָם הֲרֵי שׁוֹר שָׁחוּט לְפָנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All מגו cases should be treated alike.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מגו does not overcome evidence that already raises suspicion.

steps.title: If most women marry as בתולות, why are witnesses needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier point about witnesses. Since most women marry as בתולות, the majority should be enough even without witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since most women marry as בתולות, if witnesses did not come, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier point about witnesses. It asks why witnesses are needed at all, since most women marry as בתולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the majority (רוב) is normally strong enough to decide a case. If most brides are בתולות, we should assume this woman was one too, even with no witnesses. So why should the lack of witnesses make any difference?

keyTerms.meaning: Majority; we normally follow what is true of most cases
Marry as virgins
Witnesses

phrases.english: And since most women are married as virgins,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא אָתוּ עֵדִים מַאי הָוֵי!
phrases.english: if witnesses did not come, what of it!
phrases.notes: These are the witnesses who could show she married as a בתולה. The גמרא asks why we would need them at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דְּרוֹב נָשִׁים בְּתוּלוֹת נִישָּׂאוֹת כִּי לָא אָתוּ עֵדִים מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מגו discussion and returns to the earlier point about witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for witnesses that she married as a בתולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The majority already supports her, so witnesses seem unnecessary.

steps.title: רבינא: a virgin's wedding gets talked about
steps.stepSummary: רבינא begins his answer. Most women marry as בתולות and a minority as אלמנות, but every virgin's wedding normally gets public attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Because one can say that most women marry as בתולות and a minority as widows, and every woman who marries as a בתולה gets publicity...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts to explain why witnesses still matter despite the majority. His answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא adds a new fact: a virgin's wedding normally becomes publicly known. So the majority is not the only thing to look at. We also have to ask whether this wedding got the publicity that a virgin's wedding normally gets. The rest of his reasoning comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Minority
Widows
Publicity; the event becomes known

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Because there is room to say
most women are married as virgins,
and a minority as widows,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַנִּשֵּׂאת בְּתוּלָה — יֵשׁ לָהּ קוֹל,
phrases.english: and anyone who is married as a virgin has publicity,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds another factor (publicity) alongside the majority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The majority alone should prove she married as a בתולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a virgin's wedding normally gets publicity, we must also consider whether this wedding did. רבינא's full answer continues on the next amud.
